title: Разговор по душам в кабинете  (A Heart-to-Heart in the Office)

segments.t: Impressed by Max's work at the stove, Aleksandr invites him into the office for a mid-shift drink and asks where he learned to cook. After joking that Max should have dodged the army too, the new chef starts asking which women at Claude Monet are single.
Спасибо, шеф.
Ты где готовить учился?
О, в армии еще чему-то учат?
А ты не служил?
Но, между прочим, тебе тоже надо было сбежать.
У тебя есть потенциал?
Да, заходи.
Да я вообще-то на работе.
Да ладно, шеф разрешает.
Слушай, а расскажи мне о наших девушках.
Понял, девушка моего друга, мой враг.
А ладно, в хорошем смысле.
А вон та.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
Спасибо, шеф.

'Thank you, Chef.' Kostya promptly sends this word of thanks at this moment using "spasibo" ("thank you") — the everyday word for "thank you", which grew out of the old blessing "spasi Bog" ("God save you").
Ты где готовить учился?
'Where did you learn to cook?' Kostya questions skeptically while looking straight at Max here.
О, в армии еще чему-то учат?
'Oh, they still teach you something in the army?' Focusing on the army before Barinov, Max reaches for the Russian word "armii" ("army", built from "armiya") right at the center of the line.
А ты не служил?
'Wait, did you not serve?' Turning earnestly at once, Barinov keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for Kostya purely through rising pitch.
Но, между прочим, тебе тоже надо было сбежать.
'By the way, you should have run away from the draft too.' Kostya follows up boldly toward Barinov, refusing to let the moment slip past.
У тебя есть потенциал?
'Do you think I have potential?' Highlighting the potential right here, Max puts the emphasis on "potentsial" ("potential") in the middle of the talk.
Да, заходи.
'Yes, come on in.' Replying openly in the exchange, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Да я вообще-то на работе.
'I am actually on the clock right now.' Kostya opens up sharply during the talk, shifting the mood of the conversation in a single beat.
Да ладно, шеф разрешает.

'Come on, the Chef allows it.' Max directly gives this word of agreement beside Barinov using "ladno" ("alright") — built from the old Russian root for harmony and order, used every day for "okay, fine".
Слушай, а расскажи мне о наших девушках.

'Listen, tell me about our girls here.' Touching on the young woman right here, Barinov reaches for the Russian word "devushkakh" ("young woman", built from "devushka") right at the center of the line.
Понял, девушка моего друга, мой враг.
'Got it, pal's girlfriend is off-limits.' Kostya counters pointedly around Barinov, testing Barinov's reaction in the middle of the exchange.
А ладно, в хорошем смысле.
'All right, in the good sense.' Highlighting the good sense right here, Max reaches for the Russian word "khoroshem" ("good", built from "khoroshiy") right at the center of the line.
А вон та.
'And what about that one over there.' Following up candidly with Max, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Спасибо, шеф.
Ты где готовить учился?
О, в армии еще чему-то учат?
А ты не служил?
Но, между прочим, тебе тоже надо было сбежать.
У тебя есть потенциал?
Да, заходи.
Да я вообще-то на работе.
Да ладно, шеф разрешает.
Слушай, а расскажи мне о наших девушках.
Понял, девушка моего друга, мой враг.
А ладно, в хорошем смысле.
А вон та.

That wraps up this scene as aleksandr invites Max into the chef's office for a drink during work hours, asks about his army service, and quizzes him about which women in the restaurant are single. See you next time!
Пока!
